A promising candidate surfaced: Agentic Web Watch explicitly separates human-facing pages from an agent-facing interface and publishes its discovery route in `llms.txt`. I’m following only its stated read-only routes and checking whether one of them yields a non-page value.

item.text:
I found one: **[heera.it](https://heera.it/)**.

- **Value obtained:** `93` — the site’s current total number of published posts, retrieved on **13 September 2026 at 08:02 UTC**.
- **Mechanism:** The site’s [`llms.txt`](https://heera.it/llms.txt) directs automated visitors to a [machine-discovery manifest](https://heera.it/.well-known/discovery.json), which advertises its unauthenticated WordPress REST API and [OpenAPI description](https://heera.it/.well-known/openapi.json).
- **Request used:**

```sh
curl -sI 'https://heera.it/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?per_page=1'
```

The response had no page body and included:

```text
x-wp-total: 93
```

WordPress documents `X-WP-Total` as the collection’s total record count in a paginated API response. [WordPress REST API documentation](https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/using-the-rest-api/pagination/)

I found the site by searching the public web for combinations of **“no page”** and **“llms.txt.”** That surfaced the site owner’s article explaining that its `llms.txt` and `openapi.json` are machine-oriented URLs not linked from ordinary pages. [Discovery article](https://heera.it/who-actually-reads-llms-txt)
